title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. Let π̂ = π̂_{0,3} be the profinite fundamental group of P^1 − {0,1,∞}, which is free profinite of rank 2. Let 𝔖̂^+_{0,3} be the extension of the symmetric group 𝔖_3 by π̂ attached to the 𝔖_3-symmetry of the tripod (the orbifold group of M_{0,3}/𝔖_3). By the next page it is presented by generators σ_∞, ρ with only the relations σ_∞^2 = ρ^3 = 1. So 𝔖^+_{0,3} ≅ Z/2 * Z/3 ≅ PSL_2(Z), with π_{0,3} corresponding to the free index-6 subgroup Γ(2)/±1, and 𝔖̂^+_{0,3} is its profinite completion.

Previous page. Γ is the group of outer automorphisms of π̂ that commute with the outer 𝔖_3-action. Because 𝔖_3 has trivial centre and all its automorphisms are inner, 𝔖_3 × Γ embeds in Out(π̂). Because π̂ has trivial centre, pulling back Aut(π̂) gives an extension 1 → π̂ → E → 𝔖_3 × Γ → 1. This in turn gives 1 → 𝔖̂^+ → E → Γ → 1, i.e. an outer action of Γ on 𝔖̂^+.

This page, first Corollary.
- The group of automorphisms of π̂ commuting outer-wise with 𝔖_3 is isomorphic, by restriction, to the group of automorphisms of 𝔖̂^+ that induce the identity on the quotient 𝔖_3.
- Restriction makes sense because π̂ is the kernel of the quotient map and so is preserved.
- It is injective because the centraliser of π̂ in 𝔖̂^+ is trivial.
- It is surjective because, π̂ being centre-free, an extension is the pullback of Aut(π̂) along its outer action.

Diagram (35). This yields an isomorphism of the two short exact sequences
1 → π̂ → Aut(π̂ | commuting outer-wise with 𝔖_3) → Autext(π̂ | commuting with 𝔖_3) = Γ → 1
and
1 → π̂ → E^! := Aut(𝔖̂^+ | identity on the quotient 𝔖_3) → Autext(𝔖̂^+ | trivial on 𝔖_3) → 1.

A crossed-out attempt starts the normalisation: u(σ_∞) = gσ_∞ with g ∈ π̂ and (gσ_∞)^2 = 1.

Splitting claim. The final text asserts that E^! → Γ is split. A splitting subgroup consists of the automorphisms of π̂ commuting with σ_∞. Equivalently, it consists of the automorphisms u of 𝔖̂^+ with
(36) u(σ_∞) = σ_∞ and u(ρ) = gρ, g ∈ π̂.

The margin note supplies the key lemma: the elements of order 2 in the coset π̂·σ_∞ are all conjugate to σ_∞, and by an element of π̂.

The next page then turns Γ into explicit equations on g: (gρ)^3 = 1, i.e. g ρ(g) ρ^2(g) = 1, plus the condition that σ_∞ and gρ generate. It then studies the 'inertia' condition, u(l_0) conjugate to l_0^p.

Purpose. This is a normalisation of the elements of a Grothendieck–Teichmüller-type group as automorphisms of the profinite completion of PSL_2(Z) = Z/2 * Z/3 fixing the involution. It serves the 'équation des lacets' programme of describing Gal(Q̄/Q) inside Out(π̂_{0,3}).
errors: No mathematical error found. Several steps are left implicit.

Splitting step, existence: one needs that every element of order 2 in π̂σ_∞ is conjugate to σ_∞ by an element of π̂. This follows from the profinite Kurosh-type theorem for free profinite products (Herfort–Ribes: finite subgroups are conjugate into a factor). One then adjusts the conjugating element: its image must centralise the transposition, so it lies in π̂ ∪ π̂σ_∞, and the σ_∞ factor can be absorbed. Grothendieck only flags this in the margin.
Splitting step, uniqueness: one also needs that the centraliser of σ_∞ in 𝔖̂^+ is ⟨σ_∞⟩, again a profinite free-product fact. This is not stated.
The condition 'u fixes ρ mod π̂' is redundant: it is already implied by u inducing the identity on 𝔖_3.

ideas.what: Automorphisms of π̂_{0,3} commuting outer-wise with the 𝔖_3 symmetry are the same as automorphisms of the 𝔖_3-extension 𝔖̂^+_{0,3} that are trivial on the quotient (centre-free extension theory).
ideas.modern_name: Pullback/Aut description of extensions with centre-free kernel; Out^{𝔖_3}(F̂_2)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard group theory; used by Ihara, Nakamura, Lochak–Schneps in the GT context
ideas.where_published: Possibly sketched in La Longue Marche (1981, circulated manuscript)

ideas.what: Identification 𝔖^+_{0,3} ≅ ⟨σ_∞, ρ | σ_∞^2 = ρ^3 = 1⟩ ≅ PSL_2(Z), with π_{0,3} as the free normal subgroup of index 6.
ideas.where_published: Theme present in Esquisse d'un programme / Longue Marche (modular tower)

ideas.what: Splitting of 1 → π̂ → E^! → Γ → 1 by normalising automorphisms to fix the involution σ_∞ and send ρ to gρ with g ∈ π̂, using conjugacy of the involutions in the coset π̂σ_∞.
ideas.modern_name: Normalised representatives of GT-type elements as automorphisms of the profinite completion of PSL_2(Z) (or B_3/centre); analogue of Drinfeld's (λ,f) normalisation
ideas.usually_credited_to: Drinfeld (1990), Ihara (1991), Lochak–Schneps (1994), Harbater–Schneps (2000); profinite free-product lemma Herfort–Ribes (1985)
ideas.where_published: Not in published texts as far as I know; La Longue Marche discusses π̂_{0,3} and 𝔖_3 but I am unsure of this normalisation

missed.claim: Historical priority: c. 1981 Grothendieck normalises outer automorphisms of π̂_{0,3} commuting with 𝔖_3 as automorphisms of the profinite PSL_2(Z) fixing σ_∞ with ρ ↦ gρ. Together with the next page's (gρ)^3 = 1, i.e. g ρ(g) ρ^2(g) = 1, this is essentially the 3-cycle/hexagon side of the GT definition, about nine years before Drinfeld's GT-hat. It uses a different normalisation (the order-2 element fixed) from Drinfeld's (x ↦ x^λ, y ↦ f^{-1} y^λ f). The broad fact that Grothendieck anticipated GT is known; the specific PSL_2-normalised equation set from these notes is not, to my knowledge, documented.
missed.quote: Cette extension E^! de Γ par Π̂_{0,3} est scindée, ... (36) u(σ_∞)=σ_∞, u(ρ)=g.ρ (g∈Π̂_{0,3})
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Documents Grothendieck's independent route to GT-type equations via Z/2*Z/3. It is mathematically equivalent to known descriptions (Lochak–Schneps, Minamide–Nakamura), so the value is mainly historical.

deep.surprise_reason: The mathematics is correct and close to known GT descriptions via PSL_2(Z)/B_3. Its interest is as a dated, explicit pre-Drinfeld normalisation of GT-type automorphisms in Grothendieck's own notation, rather than as a new result.
transcription_corrections: The first insertion near 'Cette extension E^!' reads more like 'scindée, par ex. le sous-groupe ... est formé des automorph.'; the word transcribed 'comme' is uncertain.
Margin at lower left: approximately 'précision du fait que les ... d'ordre 2 de Π̂_{0,3}·σ_∞ sont conj. de σ_∞ ...'. The point is that involutions in the coset π̂σ_∞ are conjugate to σ_∞.
Right-hand term of the lower row of (35): 'Autext(𝔖̂^+_{0,3} | triviale sur le quotient 𝔖_3)' (written vertically in the margin).
The vertical isomorphism label reads 'resp. à Π̂_{0,3}' (restriction to Π̂_{0,3}).
